topic: Capped-propensity kink regularity and posterior calibration. In the iid binary-treatment unconfounded model with bounded outcomes, fix delta>1 and the intervention q_delta(1|x)=min(1,delta e(x)). Prove that its causal mean is pathwise differentiable exactly when K_delta(P)=E[tau(X)^2 1{e(X)=1/delta}]=0; derive the efficient influence function and exact branch-specific one-step remainder; establish its sharp propensity-margin rate; and prove a one-step posterior Bernstein-von Mises and pointwise credible-set coverage theorem without strong overlap for an explicit all-data histogram posterior whose draws cross the cap. When K_delta>0, prove nonregularity with a legal finite-cell tangent experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact derivation gives a propensity-outcome product plus delta E[tau|e-c|1{estimated and true cap branches disagree}], branchwise bounded denominators, the rate rho*epsilon+rho^(1+alpha), and a matching continuous-margin example; 2,450 legal cases including endpoints were checked. A density-cone proof spine supports the regularity iff, while boundary-bin localization supplies a concrete threshold-process route; generic margin powers and finite-dimensional posterior failures remain credited prior art. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove joint posterior concentration for the all-data Beta histogram with J=ceil(n^(1/3)), including uniform branch-relevant outcome contraction under unequal random arm counts, then close the finite-basis empirical-process decomposition. EARLY KILL TEST: For delta=2, e(x)=x, and constant separated Bernoulli outcome means, prove the deterministic posterior sieve and uniform corrected-signal empirical-process remainder; if this requires eliminating cap crossings or restoring strong overlap, pivot before attempting SoftBART. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_capped_propensity_kink_bvm.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the capped-propensity intervention mean is pathwise differentiable at laws with positive mass on e(X)=1/delta, including contrast cancellation on the cap atom and a legal finite-cell nonregular experiment when cancellation fails.

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly studies the stylized intervention min{1,delta e(x)}, but does not characterize regularity when the observational propensity has mass at its interior cap.
source_refs.author: Xiang Zhou and Aleksei Opacic

source_refs.claim: Its stochastic-intervention BvM theorem requires bounded first and second propensity derivatives and pointwise EIF Lipschitzness, conditions not met by a hard cap at e=1/delta.
source_refs.author: Tyler M. Schmidt and Nathan B. Wikle

source_refs.claim: For a nonsmooth optimal-treatment value, the authors prove an exceptional-law pathwise-differentiability criterion and a converse nonregularity result.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.excerpt: Díaz et al. ... show that the continuous threshold example is not pathwise differentiable.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Smooth propensity-dependent intervention theory cannot differentiate through min{1,delta e} at cap-contact laws. The banked continuous-dose LMTP result confirms that threshold-generated atoms can cause nonregularity, while the exceptional-law literature shows that a causal contrast can sometimes annihilate a nonsmooth decision term. Neither source calculates the binary capped intervention's one-sided tangent map. The first missing step is to prove that the directional kink is annihilated exactly when K_delta(P)=E[tau(X)^2 1{e(X)=1/delta}]=0, then construct a dominated finite-cell submodel respecting binary probabilities and bounded outcomes when K_delta>0.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if pathwise-differentiability theorem in terms of K_delta(P), the canonical gradient when K_delta=0, and an explicit regular finite-cell parametric submodel proving nonregularity when K_delta>0.

writing_exemplar.why: Its arc connects positivity-robust stochastic policies to semiparametric posterior calibration and clearly exposes the smoothness assumptions that a capped policy violates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Stochastic policies weaken positivity requirements -> calibrated posterior inference requires a regular target and stable EIF -> smooth propensity-dependent policies satisfy the existing theory -> the policy-natural hard cap demands an exact regularity frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute one-sided derivatives of a causal value, identify when the contrast annihilates the exceptional set, and prove the converse using a score perturbation supported there.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets compose a smooth causal law with a pointwise kink, and the required result is an exact regularity criterion rather than a sufficient condition.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate a stochastic intervention depending on the observational propensity and derive its efficient influence function and orthogonal one-step estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Away from the cap, the capped policy has the same propensity-dependent score calculus and positivity-robust weighting structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed a nondifferentiable functional in a finite-dimensional LAN experiment and translate failure of differentiability into regular-estimation impossibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A legal finite-cell cap experiment reduces the causal functional to precisely this finite-dimensional nondifferentiable setting.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a one-step posterior Bernstein-von Mises theorem and pointwise credible-set coverage for an all-data Beta/Dirichlet histogram posterior whose propensity draws may cross the cap and whose treatment-arm cell counts are unequal.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves calibrated one-step posterior inference for smooth stochastic interventions using posterior remainder and EIF empirical-process conditions that a cap-crossing signal does not automatically satisfy.
source_refs.author: Tyler M. Schmidt and Nathan B. Wikle

source_refs.claim: The authors give general sufficient conditions for a Bayesian-bootstrap one-step posterior to possess calibrated frequentist limits and specialize them to causal and missing-data functionals.
source_refs.author: Andrew Yiu, Edwin Fong, Chris Holmes, and Judith Rousseau
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper proves optimal sup-norm posterior contraction for random histograms, but not joint conditional propensity and arm-regression contraction under random unequal arm counts.
source_refs.author: Ismaël Castillo

source_refs.excerpt: On Ω_x, the exact intercept weights reproduce polynomials through degree ℓ and obey ∑|w_ix|≤C.
Conditional on N=k≥1, the selected outcomes are independent and identically distributed, supported on [0,1].

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing one-step posterior theorems require posterior remainder control and empirical-process stability of the corrected influence signal. Cap-crossing posterior draws destroy the global pointwise-Lipschitz argument. The conjugate histogram route also requires a result not supplied by general histogram-density contraction: simultaneous branch-relevant contraction of cell masses, treatment propensities, and both outcome regressions under unequal random treated and control counts. The prior proposals supply random-count conditioning, stabilization, and total zero-count fallbacks, but not the joint posterior law or the finite-basis empirical-process decomposition. Prohibiting cap crossings would remove the target phenomenon, and imposing strong overlap would abandon a central motivation for the intervention.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For J=ceil(n^(1/3)), a joint posterior contraction theorem and finite-basis stochastic-equicontinuity lemma implying bounded-Lipschitz convergence of the corrected capped-mean posterior to its efficient Gaussian law and pointwise frequentist coverage of equal-tailed credible intervals while cap crossings remain allowed.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest stochastic-policy posterior-calibration narrative and the precise smooth benchmark whose proof obligations fail for cap crossings.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Flexible Bayesian nuisance models propagate uncertainty -> raw causal target posteriors need semiparametric correction -> smooth stochastic interventions admit efficient Gaussian calibration -> cap-crossing draws require new posterior localization and empirical-process arguments.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a Bayesian-bootstrap EIF correction to posterior draws and prove BvM by separating posterior remainder, L2 influence-function stability, and empirical-process conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired posterior is a one-step corrected distribution; the new task is to verify these conditions for a branch-changing functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit conjugate histogram coordinates and multiscale concentration inequalities to obtain uniform rather than only integrated posterior contraction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform localization around e=1/delta controls the cap-crossing set, and the histogram coordinates reduce the corrected signal to a finite basis.

method_exemplars.technique: Use influence-function-motivated prior and posterior corrections to prove efficient centering and exact credible-set coverage under product-type nuisance conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how causal nuisance posterior uncertainty and orthogonal correction combine in a BvM theorem; the capped target adds a margin-controlled crossing remainder.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact branch-specific one-step remainder for the capped-propensity mean and prove that its cap-disagreement contribution has the sharp order rho^(1+alpha) under a propensity-margin condition.

source_refs.claim: Its smooth stochastic-intervention theorem controls a quadratic propensity remainder through bounded first and second derivatives, a Taylor route unavailable at the hard cap.
source_refs.author: Tyler M. Schmidt and Nathan B. Wikle

source_refs.claim: For nonsmooth causal bound functionals, the paper uses a margin condition to control branch-selection errors and recover influence-function estimation with flexible nuisance fits.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, and Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper proves sharp upper and minimax lower rates for plug-in boundary decisions under a low-noise or margin condition.
source_refs.author: Jean-Yves Audibert and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

source_refs.excerpt: A block of mass ~h^α, contrast ~h, propensity ~h^β meets the overlap-decay envelope.
the true minimax rate off it stays OPEN; the strict-deterioration comparator is a clipped-estimator surrogate

open_problems.why_unsolved: Estimated and true propensities can lie on opposite sides of 1/delta, so a global second-order Taylor bound is invalid. The residual is localized to a moving cap-disagreement set and weighted by tau(X); generic nuisance-product theory does not control it, while classification-margin results do not preserve the causal score's branch-specific denominators. The prior catalogue also shows why an upper envelope alone is insufficient: sharpness requires a legal shell-matching construction. The missing proof must derive the exact remainder before applying the margin condition and coordinate bounded outcome regressions and propensity perturbations so the lower example attains the same rho*epsilon+rho^(1+alpha) order.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact identity separating the usual propensity-outcome product from delta E[tau(X)|e_hat(X)-1/delta|1{estimated and true cap branches disagree}], followed by matching upper and lower bounds of order rho*epsilon+rho^(1+alpha) and a continuous-margin construction attaining the exponent.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames a nonsmooth causal functional by isolating the failure of ordinary efficiency arguments and making margin geometry the bridge to fast inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A policy-relevant causal target changes analytic branch -> ordinary smooth remainder calculus fails -> error localizes near the switching boundary -> a margin condition yields a sharp branch-disagreement rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Split a nonsmooth influence-function estimator into agreement and disagreement regions, then use a margin probability bound while retaining nuisance-product orthogonality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Capped policies and max/min bound endpoints both switch formula when an estimated nuisance crosses a conditional threshold.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate uniform regression error into a boundary-localized rate under a margin exponent and construct least-favorable distributions for matching lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cap-branch disagreement is a plug-in classification error for whether e(X) exceeds 1/delta, and sharpness requires calibrated mass near that boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the stochastic-intervention EIF to expose cancellation between plug-in and correction terms and isolate a nuisance-product remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the smooth component of the desired identity; the new component is the explicitly localized branch-disagreement term.

open_problems.open_problem: At positive kink-signal laws, characterize the capped mean's local Gaussian-threshold experiment and determine the sharp expected-length constant and an attaining honest confidence interval across regular, contrast-cancelled, and nonregular cap-contact sequences.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves local-unbiasedness impossibility for nondifferentiable functionals and motivates local asymptotic minimax or one-sided inference criteria.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: The authors characterize ordinary-bootstrap failure for directionally differentiable maps and construct an estimated-directional-derivative alternative.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs root-n confidence intervals for an optimal causal value at exceptional laws while recovering efficiency at regular laws.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.excerpt: does a conditional-modulus interval ... attain the sharp asymptotic minimax constant ... uniformly

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic directional-delta and impossibility results do not identify this target's tangent cone because the cap acts on a conditional treatment probability and its kink is weighted by the treatment contrast. The banked LMTP project leaves the analogous sharp interval constant and mixed regular-plus-local experiment open, but its continuous-dose atom geometry does not transfer verbatim. The first missing step is a dominated binary-treatment finite-cell embedding whose contiguous scores cross e=1/delta, followed by evaluation of the resulting min-of-Gaussian experiment's connected-interval modulus. Contrast cancellation changes the tangent cone, so an interval must adapt without losing coverage on nearby nonregular laws.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite-cell LAN representation with a directionally differentiable Gaussian-threshold limit, its fixed-level minimax connected-interval expected-length constant, and a total data-based interval attaining uniform local coverage and that constant over specified shrinking cap-contact regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats exceptional-law nonregularity as the beginning of the causal inference problem and asks what useful inference remains valid across the boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal policy value contains a pointwise kink -> exceptional strata destroy ordinary regularity -> Wald inference is unreliable near the boundary -> characterize the local experiment and construct inference valid across regular and nonregular laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce nondifferentiability to a finite-dimensional Gaussian shift experiment and derive local impossibility and minimax consequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed legal finite-cell construction is designed to turn the capped causal functional into their nondifferentiable local-experiment form.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the Hadamard directional derivative and bootstrap the derivative map instead of the original nonsmooth plug-in functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the cap's tangent map is explicit, this is the natural candidate for locally valid resampling across cap-contact sequences.

method_exemplars.technique: Evaluate an ordered modulus for a local parameter space and invert the least-favorable statistic to obtain a sharp honest interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution includes an exact fixed-level expected-length optimization in a locally constrained experiment.

literature_map:
Díaz Muñoz and van der Laan (2012, Biometrics) establish stochastic-intervention parameters, EIF estimators, and weaker positivity requirements.
Haneuse and Rotnitzky (2013, Statistics in Medicine) formalize modified treatment policies whose intervention law depends on the received-treatment mechanism.
Kennedy (2019, JASA) gives identification, efficiency theory, one-step estimation, and uniform inference for smooth incremental odds interventions without positivity.
Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi (2021, Journal of Causal Inference) extend smooth incremental interventions to many timepoints and dropout using a sequential EIF.
Díaz, Williams, Hoffman, and Schenck (2023, JASA) provide sequential identification, EIFs, and double robustness for longitudinal modified treatment policies.
Zhou and Opacic (2022, arXiv:2206.10717) explicitly study propensity multiplication until one, but not regularity at positive-mass cap contact.
Schmidt and Wikle (2026, arXiv:2608.02924) prove one-step posterior BvM calibration for smooth stochastic interventions under derivative and EIF-Lipschitz requirements that hard caps violate.
Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Annals of Statistics) give the closest causal analogue: an exact differentiability frontier and inference at exceptional optimal-rule laws.
Hirano and Porter (2012, Econometrica) establish local impossibility for nondifferentiable functionals; Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud) characterize bootstrap failure and derivative-bootstrap repair.
Audibert and Tsybakov (2007, Annals of Statistics) provide sharp margin-rate and lower-bound machinery for plug-in boundary decisions.
Levis et al. (2025, JRSSB) show how a nonsmooth causal functional can recover influence-function estimation under a margin condition.
Yiu et al. (2025, JRSSB) supply the general one-step posterior correction and isolate posterior-remainder and empirical-process obligations.
Ray and van der Vaart (2020, Annals of Statistics) and Breunig, Liu, and Yu (2025, Econometrica) provide smooth causal semiparametric BvM benchmarks.
Castillo (2014, Annals of Statistics) proves sup-norm histogram contraction, but not joint conditional Beta-histogram contraction under unequal random treatment-arm counts.
The central tension is that the capped policy is already explicit and positivity-robust, while current efficiency and posterior-calibration machinery relies on smooth intervention maps.
